shorterRoute: Use the actual integral Hecke submodule generated by original parabolic H1. The already proved original character kernel gives its character support. Native finite-module support and residue-field tensor base change supply a nonzero character fiber; the existing finite-lattice integrality argument then applies. Commutativity transports a congruence from parabolic generators to their Hecke span. The fixed finite quotient torsion annihilator controls scalar saturation. This avoids proving general integral corestriction-parabolic stability merely to obtain this necessary congruence.
assumptionsToDischarge: A finite module has a nonzero fiber for each character annihilating its annihilator; full faithfulness is unnecessary.
Divisibility of an operator on that module gives an integral quotient of the same character value.
For the original Hecke span of parabolic H1 the original Fourier-field character has the required support, and original operator congruences give the matching integrality away from one fixed integer.
remaining: The Hecke span is not asserted to equal parabolic H1. Its finite Gamma1 realization, parabolic transfer, exceptional primes, finite character descent, diamonds and arithmetic/Galois comparisons remain. No all-prime theorem is weakened. DUB17--20 OPEN;16/20 unchanged.
